name: breezeway
what_it_holds: Automated ETL syncing Breezeway API data (properties with photos, reservations with guest details, tasks, people, supplies, tags) into PostgreSQL for ~2,000 properties, ~3,500 reservations, ~15,000 tasks on average across 8 vacation-rental regions (one operator's private portfolio). No data committed to the repo itself — code/schema only.
why_useful: Possible ETL pattern for Breezeway ops data if it turns out to include sample exports, but unverified and most likely another account-specific integration script rather than a dataset.
themes: Vacation rental damage/turnover/cleaning marketplaces (Turno, TurnoverBnB), STR supply services (Airbnb photographer, key exchange) datasets
why_all: Possible ETL pattern for Breezeway ops data if it turns out to include sample exports, but unverified and most likely another account-specific integration script rather than a dataset.

Shows the shape of real STR turnover/task data one operator manages (scale: thousands of properties/tasks) but it is a private company's operational pipeline, not a public dataset, and requires their own Breezeway credentials to run.

name: homeassistant-rental-control
what_it_holds: Home Assistant integration that ingests ICS calendars from rental platforms (Airbnb, VRBO, etc.), tracks guest occupancy via a state machine, and auto-generates smart-lock door codes (key-exchange automation) via Keymaster. Test fixtures include sample ICS calendar files; no production data committed.
why_useful: A generic, reusable method for pulling a given listing's booking calendar (check-in/out dates) as ICS from Airbnb/VRBO — same underlying mechanism as the calendar files Inside Airbnb captures, but per-listing and requires the host's own private ICS URL, so not a route to market-wide data. The key-exchange/door-code angle is a real STR-supply-service touchpoint but generates no dataset.
themes: Vacation rental damage/turnover/cleaning marketplaces (Turno, TurnoverBnB), STR supply services (Airbnb photographer, key exchange) datasets

name: OpenSTR
what_it_holds: Self-hosted cleaning-management platform for STR hosts: scheduling, checklists, before/after photo evidence, supply tracking, Airbnb iCal sync, network-aware mobile app. Node/Express + React + Flutter + Postgres. Only demo/seed data (fake properties, rooms, tasks); no real datasets. 3 stars, GPL-3.0, last activity ~Apr 2026.
why_useful: Open-source alternative to Turno/Properly showing the data model (task/checklist/photo schema) an STR turnover system would use, but ships no real data and each deployment is single-operator.
themes: Vacation rental damage/turnover/cleaning marketplaces (Turno, TurnoverBnB), STR supply services (Airbnb photographer, key exchange) datasets
why_all: Open-source alternative to Turno/Properly showing the data model (task/checklist/photo schema) an STR turnover system would use, but ships no real data and each deployment is single-operator.

name: RentTools.io
what_it_holds: Open-source free property manager for STR hosts: calendar sync across Airbnb/Booking.com/Vrbo/iCal, cleaning-schedule automation, passport-data OCR extraction (Gemini), performance reporting with occupancy/ADR/revenue metrics. Booking data stored in a hosted SQLite instance, not committed to repo. 23 stars, 689 commits.
why_useful: Notable because it computes occupancy/ADR/revenue reporting across multiple booking platforms per property — again a per-operator tool, not a public dataset, but the most actively maintained (23 stars) of the open-source PMS/turnover tools found.
last_activity: recent (689 commits, active per repo page)
themes: Vacation rental damage/turnover/cleaning marketplaces (Turno, TurnoverBnB), STR supply services (Airbnb photographer, key exchange) datasets
wildcard: an Airbnb superhost / small property manager who uses open-s
why_all: Notable because it computes occupancy/ADR/revenue reporting across multiple booking platforms per property — again a per-operator tool, not a public dataset, but the most actively maintained (23 stars) of the open-source PMS/turnover tools found.

Shows the exact iCal-export mechanics (Airbnb and Booking.com both expose per-listing .ics export URLs) that any small-scale, ToS-compliant occupancy-proxy build would use; also a candidate 'better mousetrap' if the project ever wanted to invite cooperating hosts to contribute their own calendar exports for a bottom-up occupancy panel.
